subject: Post-demo: Load runbook, allowlist & test-account request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@finlytics.com>, ops+loadtest@finlytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T14:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: Load runbook, allowlist & test-account request

Great demo earlier — thanks everyone for taking the time. Quick recap and next steps so we can get the customer-led load test running next week:

Summary / goals
- Objective: Validate production-like inference throughput and latency for your Streaming Chat endpoint (model: gptx-13b-redwood).
- Targets provided by Finlytics: sustained 600 req/s, peak bursts to 1,200 req/s, p95 latency ≤ 250ms (inference), p50 ≤ 80ms; streaming chunk latency <100ms.
- Test tools: Finlytics will run Locust for session-based streaming flows; Redwood will run a smoke k6 script during the same window to confirm routing and allowlist.

Action items (owners)
1) Finlytics (Samuel / ops+loadtest): confirm final test window and provide test IP ranges for allowlist + a list of test accounts (username/password or API keys).
2) Redwood (Karthik / Dev): provide the allowlist IPs to the infra team, share runbook and k6/Locust starter scripts, and provision scoped test accounts with rate limits. Attachments: k6-script-runbook.js, locustfile.py, test-accounts.csv (see attachments).
3) Marissa: coordinate monitoring / escalation contact and confirm who at Finlytics will receive logs and access to our test dashboards.

Proposed windows (pick one):
- Wed 2026-09-08, 09:00-13:00 PT (preferred)
- Thu 2026-09-09, 14:00-18:00 PT

Notes on setup:
- We recommend using finite ramp (10m ramp, 30m sustain, 10m ramp down) rather than immediate spikes. Provide the Locust CSV userfile so we can mirror traffic patterns.
- For streaming tests, ensure client-side backpressure is disabled so we can measure chunk latency and token streaming behaviour.

Please reply with the confirmed window and the IP ranges. I attached the starter scripts and the runbook for reference.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@finlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+loadtest@finlytics.com, Liu Wei <l.wei@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Load runbook, allowlist & test-account request

Thanks Karthik — the targets look right. A few clarifications and what we can provide:

1) Test window: Wed 2026-09-08, 09:00-13:00 PT works for us.
2) IP ranges for our test cluster: 34.82.120.0/24, 34.82.121.0/24 (these are the egress ranges for our ephemeral k8s workers). Please confirm if you need single IPs or CIDR blocks.
3) We'll run Locust for streaming sessions (script will use websocket-based load). We'll also produce a Locust CSV of user journeys and share it by EOD Tue 2026-09-07.
4) Test accounts: we'll send a csv with 50 test API keys and a single shared test org id. For security, we'll rotate keys after the run.

One ask: for the streaming endpoint, can Redwood enable a higher per-connection concurrent token limit for this org for the test (we're planning long-lived connections ~30s avg). If that's a config you can toggle on a per-org basis, please let us know how to request it.

Sam
Samuel Ortiz
SRE Lead, Finlytics
samuel.ortiz@finlytics.com
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@finlytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T01:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Load runbook, allowlist & test-account request

On Thu, Sep 1, 2026 at 17:05, Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@finlytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks Karthik — the targets look right. A few clarifications and what we can provide:
>
> 1) Test window: Wed 2026-09-08, 09:00-13:00 PT works for us.
>
Thanks Sam. Quick notes from infra / ops side: we can accept the two CIDR blocks as-is for the allowlist. Please also provide any outbound webhook target IPs if Locust workers will be calling back to Finlytics dashboards.

Regarding the streaming per-connection token limit: we can set a temporary policy for the test org (RDW-FT-TEST) to increase the per-connection token cap and max concurrent streams per connection. We need the test org id and an approximate max concurrent streams value (you suggested avg 1 stream per user, up to 20 concurrent streams per worker pod). If you can give a headcount estimate we will configure limits accordingly.

I've uploaded a short runbook and two starter scripts to the thread as attachments (k6-script-runbook.js, locustfile.py) and created 50 scoped API keys for test org RDW-FT-TEST. I'll share the test-accounts.csv separately via the secure link in our Drive.

Dev
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@finlytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Load runbook, allowlist & test-account request

Looping in monitoring and the escalation playbook:
- Monitoring: I'll provision dashboard access to Finlytics SREs with read-only view and realtime alert hooks. Expect an invite to our Grafana instance before the test.
- Emergency contact: For any severe degradation we'll open the #finlytics-loadtest Slack channel and call the on-call. Please confirm the primary Finlytics on-call (Samuel?).

Also: reminder to stick to the proposed ramp plan and to avoid running production traffic. We'll snapshot logs and retain them for 30 days per the mutual action plan.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Liu Wei <l.wei@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Load runbook, allowlist & test-account request

Thanks all — confirming the last details from our end:

- Final window confirmed: 2026-09-08 09:00-13:00 PT.
- IP allowlist confirmed: 34.82.120.0/24, 34.82.121.0/24. We'll send a signed PoLP (principle of least privilege) confirmation to security if required.
- Concurrent streams: average 1 stream per virtual user, max 20 concurrent streams per worker, approx 500 worker pods for peak -> this maps to your peak 1,200 req/s number.
- Locust artifacts: we've uploaded the locustfile and scenario CSV to S3 (https://s3-finlytics-public/locust/ft-scenarios/sep08). We'll share the presigned links with you now.
- Test account CSV: attached via secure Drive link (see doc link). We'll rotate keys after completion.

One small ask: can Redwood confirm the expected token billing behavior for test traffic (i.e., tokens counted vs. waived for scoped test org)? We want to ensure we won't incur unexpected costs.

Liu Wei
Finlytics SRE
l.wei@finlytics.com
